newsitem.title: USA: Morton Intl Q3 net up on tough comparison.
newsitem.headline: Morton Intl Q3 net up on tough comparison.

text.p: Morton International Inc reported a one-percent increase in net income for the March 31 third quarter over the same year-ago period. The company said a one-time year-ago item affected year-over-year comparisons.

The 1996 results included a one-time receipt of $15 million ($9.4 million after tax) from its joint venture partner, Nippon Paint Co, for creation of Morton Nippon Coatings. Per share earnings were up six percent to $0.76.
Excluding the impact of the joint venture, earnings per share rose 15 percent. Sales in the quarter grew three percent to $1.03 billion.

"Although our salt business had lower sales for the quarter following last year's extremely harsh winter in the United States, earnings improved due to the winter in Canada and tight cost controls," said chairman S. Jay Stewart.

"Specialty chemicals results were positively impacted by the acquisition of Pulverlac, an Italian powder coatings business, and strong U.S. results in several product areas," Stewart added. However, results were hurt by currency translation and soft European sales.

"Price declines and slowing automobile production during the latter part of the quarter affected the performance of the airbag business, although operating margins improved to 19 percent," said Stewart in a statement.

Morton continued to buy back shares and is close to completing its 10 million share authorization, Stewart added, observing that "Average lower shares outstanding also helped improved earnings per share.
